question: How has NVIDIA's revenue and growth outlook changed over the last two years?

summary.text: NVIDIA's revenue scale roughly doubled twice in two years: fiscal 2024 revenue was $60.9 billion, up 126% from a year ago, and fiscal 2025 total revenue reached $130,497 million versus $60,922 million in fiscal 2024.

Growth has stayed steep but is decelerating in percentage terms: third-quarter fiscal 2026 revenue was $57,006 million against $35,082 million a year earlier, with nine-month revenue of $147,811 million versus $91,166 million (about 62% growth).

The driver of the outlook has rotated from Hopper to Blackwell, which entered production shipment in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, with nine-month fiscal 2026 Data Center computing up 59% and networking up 105% year over year.
The excerpts carry no management revenue guidance figures, so the forward outlook is described qualitatively rather than quantified.

claims.text: NVIDIA fiscal year 2024 revenue was $60.9 billion, up 126% from a year ago.
claims.quote: Revenue for fiscal year 2024 was $60.9 billion, up 126% from a year ago.

claims.text: NVIDIA total revenue was $130,497 million in fiscal 2025, versus $60,922 million in fiscal 2024 and $26,974 million in fiscal 2023.
NVIDIA revenue was $57,006 million in the quarter ended Oct 26, 2025 versus $35,082 million a year earlier, and $147,811 million for the nine months versus $91,166 million.
NVIDIA began shipping production systems of the Blackwell architecture in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025, after Hopper demand drove full-year fiscal 2025 growth.
claims.quote: Demand for our Hopper architecture drove our significant growth for the full year. We began shipping production systems of the Blackwell architecture in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025.

claims.text: For the first nine months of fiscal 2026, NVIDIA Data Center computing revenue grew 59% year on year and Data Center networking revenue grew 105% year on year.
claims.quote: Revenue from Data Center computing grew 59% year-on-year compared to the first nine months of fiscal year 2025, driven by demand for our Blackwell computing platform. Revenue from Data Center networking grew 105% year-on-year
